title: How to Reduce Registration Shift in Foil Stamping

seo.title: How to Reduce Registration Shift in Foil Stamping

content:
Registration shift happens when the foil position does not align with the printed artwork, border, embossing area or package layout. It is especially noticeable on cosmetic boxes, labels and premium paper packaging.

## Main Causes

The first cause is sheet movement during feeding. Paper curl, static, thickness variation or unstable feeding can move the sheet slightly before stamping.

The second cause is setup alignment. If the stamping plate is not positioned accurately, the shift may appear in the same direction throughout the run.

The third cause is artwork tolerance. Designs that place foil exactly on a thin printed outline leave very little room for normal production variation.

## How to Diagnose

Check whether the shift is consistent or random. A consistent shift usually points to setup or artwork alignment. A random shift usually points to feeding or sheet stability.

## How to Reduce Risk

Allow realistic tolerance in the design. Avoid placing foil on extremely tight printed outlines when possible. For multi-process packaging, test the full production sequence.

## FAQ

### Is registration shift caused by foil quality?

Usually not directly. It is more often related to feeding, setup or artwork tolerance.

### How can designers reduce the risk?

Use practical spacing and avoid over-tight foil-to-print alignment.
